findings.source_quote: spero autem omnes qui iam antea peccaverunt, si haec audiant, quod libenter acturi sunt paenitentiam, vitam recuperantes.
findings.english_quote: I hope everyone who sinned before will hear these things, gladly repent, and regain life.
findings.issue: The conditional clause “si haec audiant” (“if they hear these things”) becomes an additional object of hope: that everyone will hear. This removes the source’s expressed condition and changes the scope of the speaker’s hope. The standard edition retains the condition, but the simplified edition does not.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed for fresh review: “But I hope that everyone who sinned before, if they hear these things, will gladly repent and regain life.” Retain hearing as a condition rather than as a separately hoped-for event.

summary: Both editions were reviewed clause by clause against the selected edited Latin. The standard is acceptable within that scope; the simplified needs revision to restore the condition in section 3. Both preserve contextual repentance, the life/death assertions, negations, blood-guilt, and remedy language. The notes disclose the elliptical supplements, the alternative interpretation of hic, and the reported textual variant without requiring replacement of the working reading. Acceptance does not authenticate unseen manuscripts, independently verify the cited apparatus or catalogue, or certify exhaustive collation. Any proposed replacement requires fresh review.
